turns.assessment: The two earliest network alarms are simultaneous AMP_INPUT_LOS at the first inline amplifiers on S01→S04 and S01→S15, while the upstream boosters and amplifier pump currents show no change. That localizes the loss ahead of those inline amplifiers and argues strongly against amplifier failure; a fibre-cut event affecting co-routed cables is most plausible. For svc300, the S01→S15-side cut is the likelier interrupting fault, but the actual span is only expressible relative to O2 and no single named repairable element is established strongly enough for commitment.

proposals.rationale: O2 reports input LOS at the first inline amplifier on S01→S15 while the preceding booster retained normal input/output power and pump current. This is the signature of loss in the fibre between the booster and inline amplifier and is the most relevant observed cut for svc300.

The identical simultaneous input-LOS condition on S01→S04, despite normal upstream booster behavior, indicates another likely fibre cut. Documentation explicitly notes that excavation can cut other cables in the same duct.

ROADM S01 is the sole listed common dependency and a WSS input-port failure can affect many channels. However, unchanged booster input/output power downstream of S01 is evidence against the ROADM having removed all optical signal, whereas the inline-amplifier input LOS localizes beyond the boosters.
